gopdfgo at a glance: comparison with Chromium, unsupported features, requirements

gopdfgo turns HTML, CSS and SVG into PDF in pure Go. It needs no browser and runs no JavaScript. It supports CSS Paged Media: pages, margins, margin boxes with headers and footers, page counters and breaks. It is built for ordinary business documents (invoices, reports, financial statements, multi-page tables), not for printing arbitrary web pages.

All numbers below were measured on 2026-11-20:

  • gopdfgo: commit e3f59aa (code as of this page's first version), engine gopdfgo/webrender 0.1.0-dev;
  • Chromium: Google Chrome 157.0.8103.79 on macOS;
  • browser size on a server: Chrome 158.0.8127.36 on Ubuntu.

They need to be measured again after engine changes.

Size

Chromium gopdfgo
software browser: 460 MB on a Linux server (du -sh /opt/google/chrome) plus system libraries from packages; 2.2 GB on macOS 21.2 MB command-line binary, linux/amd64, CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w"
fonts system fonts supplied by the caller (in xml.pro: 2.1 MB, five Noto files)
installation and updates browser package, security updates, a writable home directory for the browser process one static binary, nothing to install on the system

Speed and memory

Documents:

  • four variants of a Polish KSeF e-invoice as printed by an e-invoice viewer: 1, 3, 1 and 7 pages;
  • five e-SF financial statements from the public Polish court register (KRS), labelled A–E: 6, 11, 12, 16 and 4 pages.

Both engines got the same font files (Noto Sans, Noto Sans Mono). All nine documents have the same page count in both engines.

Machine: Apple M4, 10 cores, 32 GB, system load average 6.7–7.9 during the run. Times are the shortest of five runs of the whole process, including program start.

Document Pages Chromium, --headless --print-to-pdf (browser starts for each document) gopdfgo, command line
invoice, 2 items 1 409 ms 49 ms
invoice, 60 items 3 426 ms 73 ms
invoice, VAT rates and bank transfer 1 407 ms 53 ms
invoice, 140 items 7 469 ms 109 ms
e-SF A 6 476 ms 128 ms
e-SF B 11 534 ms 202 ms
e-SF C 12 512 ms 197 ms
e-SF D 16 547 ms 244 ms
e-SF E 4 462 ms 93 ms

Chromium kept running and driven through DevTools (Page.printToPDF via chromedp, no wait before printing) needed 0.42–0.46 s per document. That run used the same day and the same documents; see docs/chromium-comparison.md (Polish). gopdfgo is 2 to 9 times faster than that.

Memory:

  • gopdfgo, peak RSS of the process (/usr/bin/time -l): invoice 48 MB, 6-page e-SF 95 MB, 16-page e-SF 156 MB;
  • Chromium: peak RSS summed over the browser processes, 943–961 MB, with two browser instances running at once, as in xml.pro.

gopdfgo renders one document at a time per process; further calls wait in a queue. Chromium can print several tabs in parallel.

A large document: an illustrated book (256 pages)

The illustrated HTML edition of Pride and Prejudice from Project Gutenberg (book 1342, 164 illustrations by Hugh Thomson, 0.8 MB of HTML and 27 MB of JPEG/PNG images; public domain). The files are not in the repository; testdata/books/fetch.sh downloads them from the Gutenberg mirror and checks their SHA-256 sums, so the measurement can be repeated on the same input. For the measurement both engines get testdata/books/bench.css: the same font (Tinos, with Times metrics, from testdata/fonts) and A4 pages with 20 mm margins.

Measured 2026-11-20 on the same machine; gopdfgo at commit 0eb174f, Chrome 157.0.8103.79. Three runs each, whole process including program or browser start.

Chromium, --headless --print-to-pdf gopdfgo, command line
pages 253 256
time 2.13–2.47 s 1.60 s (1.54–1.58 s before the memory optimisations below)
peak memory 1672–1701 MB (all browser processes) 423–456 MB (after the optimisations below)
PDF size 27.58 MB (tagged PDF) 26.25 MB
of which images 25.21 MB (171 image objects) 24.76 MB (164 image objects)
of which text, pages, fonts and structure 2.37 MB 1.49 MB
  • Both engines embed the illustrations almost unchanged, so most of the file is images. Without them, gopdfgo's file is 37% smaller; part of that is the structure tree Chrome's command line adds for screen readers (tagged PDF). Chrome without tags (through DevTools) was not measured for this book.
  • The split was measured by summing the stream lengths of image objects, font files and everything else in the PDF.

Page count. The first measurement gave 265 pages. The cause was a bug: an @font-face rule without a font-weight descriptor got weight 0 instead of the font's own weight (auto, CSS Fonts 4 § 4.5), so normal text matched the bold face of the same family and the whole book was set in bold. After the fix the text of every page matches Chrome's up to page 30, where the first such paragraph occurs. The remaining 3 pages come from widows and orphans: Chrome splits a three-line paragraph 2 + 1 at a page end, although the initial widows: 2 forbids a single line at the top of the next page (CSS Fragmentation 3 § 3.3); with four or more lines Chrome follows the rule. gopdfgo follows the specification and moves such a paragraph whole. With widows: 1; orphans: 1 gopdfgo gives 253 pages, the same as Chrome.

Memory. The illustrations are not the cause: they are embedded without decoding, and the raw files take 27 MB of the heap. All pages are laid out before any is drawn (the design inherited from WeasyPrint), so memory grows with the number of pages. Live heap after a forced collection, measured at each stage:

Stage book, 256 pages book ×4, 1021 pages
HTML parsed, stylesheets 40 MB 47 MB
computed styles 57 MB 85 MB
box tree (the whole input) 103 MB 191 MB
all pages laid out 289 MB 527 MB
all pages drawn 390 MB 859 MB

The Go garbage collector lets the heap grow to about twice the live size before collecting (GOGC=100), which gives the peak of about 1 GB for the book. With GOGC=50 the peak was 740 MB and with GOGC=25 660 MB; wall time stays about the same, CPU time grows by 25% and 70%.

The table was measured before five optimisations, which give byte-identical output:

  • laid-out lines keep their glyphs in a compact form (44 B per glyph instead of the 80 B record of the go-text shaper);
  • justification stores only the changed glyphs instead of copying each justified line (190 MB of copies for the 1021-page book);
  • each page's boxes are released right after the page is drawn;
  • each page is drawn as soon as its layout is final; margin boxes are added to its content after all pages are laid out, so "page X of Y" needs no second pass (ADR 0027);
  • the cache of broken lines has a size limit (two generations of about 16 MB each) instead of growing for the whole document. Its key is the remaining text of the paragraph, so it took about 400 MB for 1021 pages.

Peak memory after the first four: book 0.92–1.07 → 0.56–0.63 GB, book ×4 (1021 pages, 4.8 s, Chromium 2.44 GB) 2.25–2.31 → 0.90–0.96 GB. After the fifth (measured 2026-11-21, three runs): book 0.51–0.58 → 0.42–0.46 GB, same time; book ×4 0.83–0.85 → 0.73–0.79 GB, but 4.8 → 6.4 s, because the ×4 file repeats the same text four times and the unlimited cache reused whole paragraphs from earlier copies. On a 1021-page variant with different text in each copy (one vowel replaced per copy) time is the same, 6.5 s, and memory drops from 1.30–1.54 to 0.73 GB.

Memory is now bounded mainly by the input (styles, box tree, images) rather than by the laid-out document; the peak is reached during layout.

Documents that need a second pagination pass, such as a table of contents with target-counter() or "page X of Y" with counter(pages) in the page content (not in margin boxes), are laid out twice (ADR 0036): the first pass settles page numbers and the page count and releases each page right after laying it out; the second lays out every page again with those values and draws it at once. Output is byte-identical. Documents of up to 32 pages are laid out whole, as before, because the second pass costs time and would save little memory there. Measured 2026-11-21 (three runs) on a variant of the book with a table of contents of 61 chapter links at the front and "page X of Y" under every chapter heading:

book, no TOC book with TOC, before book with TOC, after book ×4 with TOC, before book ×4 with TOC, after
pages 256 259 259 1027 1027
peak memory 440–483 MB 598–613 MB 472–479 MB 1450–1531 MB 802–839 MB
time 1.60 s 2.24 s 3.00–3.02 s 8.93–8.94 s 12.27–12.34 s

The extra layout pass costs 35–38% of time. A few cases still lay out the whole document before drawing: a positioned box continued on an earlier page, a position: fixed box that first appears on a later page, and a margin box with a negative z-index.

The inherited pagination loop marked a page with a reference to an anchor for another layout pass every time the anchor was laid out, even when its page number had not changed; the book with a table of contents ran 8 pagination passes (the limit) instead of 3. Pages are now marked only when the value changes (output is byte-identical). target-counter(…, pages) now gives the page count of the document, as CSS Generated Content 3 requires, instead of the page count of the pass in which the anchor was laid out (often 0, "3/0"); such documents now take the two-pass path too. Measured 2026-11-21 (three runs):

passes peak memory, before peak memory, after time, before time, after
book, no TOC — 431–452 MB 439–469 MB 1.61–1.63 s 1.62–1.63 s
book with TOC (259 pages) 8 → 3 467–478 MB 461–493 MB 3.04–3.06 s 2.72–2.76 s
book ×4 with TOC (1027 pages) 8 → 3 804–889 MB 834–931 MB 12.40–12.44 s 10.88–10.92 s

Current state compared with Chromium (2026-11-21)

Measured 2026-11-21 on the same machine, Chrome 157 and gopdfgo after the speed-ups of ADR 0037 (the earlier gopdfgo times, commit a655fcd, are in that ADR); three runs each, whole process including program or browser start; memory is the peak resident size, for Chromium summed over all its processes. The table-of-contents variants (61 chapter links with target-counter() at the front, "page X of Y" with counter(pages) under every chapter heading) are made by a script from the book.

Document Pages, Chromium / gopdfgo Chromium: time gopdfgo: time Chromium: memory gopdfgo: memory
book 253 / 256 2.10–2.56 s 1.17–1.22 s 1.67–1.73 GB 0.42–0.44 GB
book with table of contents 256 / 259 2.09–2.12 s 2.23–2.31 s 1.42–1.45 GB 0.44–0.46 GB
book ×4 1009 / 1021 4.54–4.69 s 4.57–4.69 s 2.20–2.26 GB 0.73–0.77 GB
book ×4 with table of contents 1015 / 1027 4.55–4.68 s 8.6–8.8 s 2.11–2.14 GB 0.78–0.80 GB
  • Chromium does not support target-counter() or counter(pages) outside margin boxes: its table of contents has no page numbers and "page X of Y" reads "Strona 0 z 0". gopdfgo writes "Chapter I — strona 20" and "Strona 11 z 259", which costs the second layout pass (ADR 0036). The times of the table-of-contents rows therefore do not compare the same work.
  • On the plain book gopdfgo takes about half of Chromium's time, partly because Chromium starts a browser for each document; at 1021 pages the two take the same time. gopdfgo's time grows linearly with the number of pages (1.2 s × 4 ≈ 4.6 s), Chromium's more slowly, so on still longer documents Chromium would lead. gopdfgo uses 2.7–3.8 times less memory in every case.
  • The extra pages come from widows (see "Page count" above): gopdfgo moves a three-line paragraph whole where Chromium splits it 2 + 1.

PDF file size

Document Chromium via DevTools (untagged PDF) Chromium --print-to-pdf (tagged PDF) gopdfgo (untagged PDF)
invoice, 2 items 26.8 kB 42.7 kB 24.9 kB
invoice, 60 items 37.5 kB 182.9 kB 35.9 kB
invoice, VAT rates and bank transfer 28.2 kB 63.3 kB 26.6 kB
invoice, 140 items 52.9 kB 383.0 kB 51.0 kB
e-SF A — 315.4 kB 60.3 kB
e-SF B — 621.9 kB 97.4 kB
e-SF C — 541.9 kB 94.0 kB
e-SF D — 734.5 kB 116.3 kB
e-SF E — 181.9 kB 40.4 kB

Chrome's command line writes a tagged PDF: it adds a structure tree for screen readers, and pdfinfo shows „Tagged: yes”. Through DevTools, with default settings, Chrome writes an untagged PDF, like gopdfgo. Those two are comparable, and gopdfgo's files are 4–7% smaller. The e-SF statements were not measured through DevTools with the same fonts.

gopdfgo writes a tagged PDF with Options.Tagged (ADR 0033); its objects then go into compressed object streams. Measured 2026-11-21 (median of 5 runs, whole process, macOS arm64): corpus invoice (20-invoice) 28.5 → 34.7 kB, register table (02-register-table, 1466 structure elements) 81.1 → 106.0 kB, mixed report (21-mixed-report) 37.7 → 35.1 kB; rendering 1–4% longer.

gopdfgo's file size comes from:

  • zlib compression at level 6 (ADR 0023);
  • font subsets that keep only the glyphs used and short tables.

Options.Uncompressed writes an uncompressed file for reading in a text editor.

Output compared with Chromium

Real documents, measured 2026-11-21 with pdftotext -bbox, words matched by sequence alignment; both engines get the same Noto fonts through @font-face; Chrome 157.

  • KSeF invoices (4): same pages; every word lies within 0.81 pt of its position in Chromium, median 0.14–0.23 pt.
  • e-SF statements from xml.pro (5, variant without scripts): same pages and page breaks; every word lies within 0.43 pt of Chromium (3 words in one statement are matched to a neighbouring row because Chrome writes that row in a different order). Before 2026-11-21 two of them had 1342–1491 words more than 3 pt away: Chromium computes layout in 1/64 px units (LayoutUnit), and gopdfgo now does the same by default (ADR 0013).
  • The remaining median of about 0.2 pt comes from Chrome snapping text baselines to whole pixels when it draws; gopdfgo keeps the exact baseline.
  • W3C screen reftests across 11 CSS areas: 9502 of 10962 pass.
  • W3C print reftests: 310 of 340 pass, 308 exactly and 2 within anti-aliasing edges (ADR 0003).
  • Own corpus of 22 documents: page counts as in Chromium; PDF/A-2b and, with tags, PDF/A-2a valid in veraPDF for 22 of 22; PDF/UA-1 valid for 22 of 22 (five documents had a skipped heading level or SVG images without alternative text; fixed in the source on 2026-11-21 without changing their pages).

Where the specifications leave a choice, gopdfgo follows Chromium; each such case is recorded in docs/adr/. Options.ExactLengths turns off the pixel and 1/64 px rounding that imitates Chromium (ADR 0013).

Not supported in this version

Out of scope by design:

  • JavaScript and everything that depends on it; video, audio; canvas stays empty. Documents embedded with iframe, object and embed are printed at the size of the element, clipped, as Chromium prints them;
  • system fonts: only the fonts supplied by the caller are used, so the output is reproducible;
  • vertical writing (writing-mode) and bidirectional or right-to-left text (ADR 0010);
  • state pseudo-classes (:hover and similar), @container, @property, ::selection;
  • structure inside SVG images, notes and references (Note, Reference) and alternative text for generated content in tagged PDF. Tagged PDF works since 2026-11-21, off by default (Options.Tagged, ADR 0033): a structure tree from the HTML elements in document order (Document, Div/Sect/Art, P, H1–H6, L/LI with Lbl for the ::marker and LBody, Table/THead/TBody/TFoot/TR/TH/ TD with Scope, RowSpan and ColSpan and the same grid as in HTML, Link with a reference to its annotation and the link text as the annotation's /Contents, Figure with Alt from alt, aria-label, the SVG <title> or the figcaption of a figure holding one image, figure as Div with Caption, Span for inline elements), marked page content, backgrounds, borders and shadows as artifacts, margin boxes and repeated table headers as pagination artifacts, /Lang from lang, the document title shown by the viewer. PDF/A-2a and PDF/A-3a turn it on; veraPDF accepts all 22 corpus documents as PDF/A-2a. PDF/UA-1 (Options.Accessibility, -pdfua 1, also together with PDF/A-2a) adds pdfuaid to the XMP metadata; veraPDF accepts 22 of 22 corpus documents. Defects gopdfgo does not repair (no title, no language, an image without alternative text, a skipped heading level, table rows with different numbers of columns) give warnings. PDF/A-2b, PDF/A-3b and file attachments are supported (ADR 0016, 0026), and so are Factur-X 1.0 / ZUGFeRD 2.x hybrid invoices (Options.FacturX, ADR 0034: the invoice XML, the fx XMP properties with their extension schema, PDF/A-3b or 3a). When rendering, gopdfgo does not validate the invoice XML against the profile's XSD or Schematron; the caller should do that. The output was checked with the Mustang validator 2.26.0 on our own MINIMUM-profile invoice (ADR 0034);
  • PNG or SVG output: the output is PDF only;
  • digital signatures (PAdES) and PDF forms.

Experimental features that browsers do not generally support yet: grid-lanes (masonry), column-height, flex-wrap: balance.

Not done yet (status and priority in docs/progress.md, Polish):

  • subgrid;
  • baseline alignment in grid and flex (last baseline, column axis);
  • some cases of positioned grid items and nested multi-column layout;
  • CSS filter: the colour functions are exact on colours and on raster image pixels; drop-shadow() and blur() are vector approximations (soft-mask copies); url() filters on HTML elements, backdrop-filter and the filter() image function are not supported;
  • perspective projection: perspective(), the perspective property and the perspective components of matrix3d() are accepted with a warning and ignored, so the element is drawn as an orthographic projection; preserve-3d has no depth sorting or plane intersection. 3D transforms without perspective (rotateX(), rotate3d(), translate3d(), matrix3d() …) and backface-visibility are exact;
  • <angle> values inside calc() in transform functions;
  • colours outside the sRGB gamut (color(display-p3 …), oklch() …) are clipped per channel, as Chromium prints them, not gamut-mapped as CSS Color 4 § 13 describes;
  • the colour of -webkit-text-stroke;
  • CSS zoom; mask and mask-image on HTML elements (masks inside SVG work); animations and transitions are not evaluated, so print shows the static style;
  • a box with overflow: hidden and a fixed height, or with contain: size, taller than a page is clipped at the page edge;
  • the frozen-item rule for column flex containers works only without wrapping;
  • hyphenation dictionaries (hyphens: auto) are built in for 24 languages: af, be, bg, da, de, el, en, es, et, fr, gl, it, lt, mn, nb, nl, nn, pl, pt, sk, sl, sq, te, uk. Other languages need a dictionary passed in Options.Hyphenation (ADR 0024).

SVG

Checked 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21 in the code (internal/webrender/svg), on the W3C svg/ reftests, and on a corpus of 23 real-world SVG files (testdata/svg: icons, flags and coats of arms from Wikimedia Commons, charts, a draw.io-style diagram) compared with Chrome 157.

Supported:

  • shapes: rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, path;
  • structure:
    • g, nested svg, defs, a;
    • use and symbol, also from another file (<use href="icons.svg#id">); the copied content inherits from the <use> element, as in a shadow tree;
    • switch with conditional attributes;
  • image (raster and SVG), foreignObject (HTML content laid out in the given box);
  • coordinates: viewBox (a zero width or height disables rendering), preserveAspectRatio, transform, also on the outermost <svg>; overflow other than visible (including auto) clips;
  • painting:
    • fill and stroke with opacity, dash arrays, line caps and joins, vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke;
    • paint servers: linearGradient, radialGradient, pattern, also taking stops or content from another one through href, as files from Inkscape and Illustrator do;
    • clipPath, mask (also with objectBoundingBox content units), marker with orient="auto", context-fill/context-stroke;
  • text: text, tspan, textPath (on a path or a path attribute, with startOffset), shaped like HTML text (kerning, ligatures, OpenType features), text-anchor per text chunk, textLength/lengthAdjust, dominant-baseline, letter-spacing, text-shadow; text is written as runs, so it can be selected and searched in the PDF;
  • styling: presentation attributes, style attributes, <style> inside the SVG and, for inline <svg> in HTML, the page's whole cascade (<style> in <head>, <link rel=stylesheet>, the user stylesheet, @media, var()), with inheritance from the HTML ancestors; var() also works in presentation attributes (r="var(--r)"); on the outermost <svg>, mask is applied by the SVG renderer and opacity, filter, clip-path and mix-blend-mode by the CSS box;
  • inline <svg> in HTML, and SVG files used with img, object, embed and CSS background-image:
    • SVG files are parsed as XML;
    • an SVG file used as an image (img, CSS images, <image>) is static and loads no external resources, only data: URLs (ADR 0031); in object/embed it loads them. Its @font-face rules and the root element's background-image work, scoped to that file;
    • a file with width and height but no viewBox stretches to the image box in img and backgrounds, and stays unscaled in object/embed, as in Chrome;
    • URL fragments select part of an image (ADR 0030): #xywh=x,y,w,h (also pixel: and percent:, Media Fragments URI 1.0) crops raster and SVG images, and #svgView(viewBox(…);preserveAspectRatio(…); transform(…)) or the name of a <view> element picks the view of an SVG file; the file is loaded once for all its fragments;
    • an SVG file used many times (a logo in every page header, icons in table rows, a background) is written once as a PDF form XObject and referenced from each use, like a raster image (ADR 0028): a 100 kB coat of arms on 41 pages gives a 68 kB PDF instead of 1.5 MB (measured 2026-11-21);
  • links: <a href> (or xlink:href) becomes a PDF link annotation covering the bounding box of its drawn content after all transforms (ADR 0029). In inline <svg>, #id links go to anchors in the HTML document and other links are external; in object/embed only external links are kept; SVG in img and CSS images is static, so it has no links. Rotated content gets its bounding rectangle, not QuadPoints.

Not supported or incomplete:

  • filters: drop shadow and blur (feGaussianBlur, feOffset, feFlood, feComposite, feMerge, feDropShadow, feBlend, feColorMatrix/feComponentTransfer on shadows) are drawn without rasterization. A blur is many soft-mask copies, so it is an approximation, within a few brightness levels of Chrome, and adds about 2 kB per filtered element. Colour matrices on the element itself and feImage, feTile, feMorphology, feTurbulence, feConvolveMatrix, lighting and feDisplacementMap skip the filter as a whole;
  • currentColor passed through a context paint, and objectBoundingBox paint servers on a context;
  • CSS zoom;
  • structure inside SVG in tagged PDF: an SVG image is one Figure with alternative text;
  • animation (SMIL), scripting and CSS Linked Parameters (a proposal) are out of scope.

W3C reftests in svg/ (687 in total): 235 can run here. The rest need scripts (44) or missing files (46), or have no reference. Of those 235, 194 pass (2026-11-21); on the morning of 2026-11-20 it was 83.

Each stand-alone .svg test was measured as a document drawn through <img>.

Remaining failures (41), the largest groups: CSS Linked Parameters (23, a proposal), CSS zoom (6), the animated state in print and use in print (6), and single cases (mask on HTML elements, path bearing commands from an SVG 2 draft, :visited). Two text-shadow tests differ from their references within the tolerance the tests declare (fuzzy), which the survey does not apply.

Real-world corpus: every file is within 2.3% of Chrome's pixels; the remaining differences are font substitution, the missing blur shadow, and anti-aliasing.

Requirements

  • Go 1.26 or newer (go.mod: go 1.26.0); built and tested with go1.26.6.
  • No cgo: builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 for any platform Go supports (checked: darwin/arm64, linux/amd64).
  • TrueType or OpenType fonts from the caller (Options.Fonts). The fonts for generic families (sans-serif, serif, monospace) are set in Options.GenericFamilies (ADR 0005).
  • External resources (stylesheets, images, @font-face fonts) come from the caller through Options.Resolver. By default the engine reads nothing from the network or the disk.
  • Module dependencies, all pure Go:
Module Licence Used for
github.com/go-text/typesetting BSD-3-Clause or Unlicense text shaping, fonts, segmentation
github.com/benoitkugler/pdf MIT PDF data structures
github.com/benoitkugler/pstokenizer MIT PostScript tokenizer (through pdf)
github.com/hhrutter/lzw BSD-3-Clause LZW filter (through pdf)
golang.org/x/image BSD-3-Clause image decoding
golang.org/x/net BSD-3-Clause HTML5 parser
golang.org/x/text BSD-3-Clause character encodings
github.com/benoitkugler/textlayout MIT tests only
  • Tools needed only for tests:
    • pdftotext and pdftoppm (Poppler);
    • Ghostscript, for the pixel tests of internal/goweasyprint/pdf;
    • veraPDF, optional, for PDF/A validation.

How it was measured

  • Time: shortest of five runs of the whole process.
    • Chromium: "Google Chrome" --headless --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf=…, a new process for each document.
    • gopdfgo: gopdfgo -fonts … -in … -out ….
  • Memory: /usr/bin/time -l, „maximum resident set size”.
  • File size: stat. Tagging: pdfinfo.
  • Program size: ls of the binary built with the command in the table above. Browser size: du -sh.
  • The source documents and the outputs are kept outside the repository.
